scope: All nine completed development episodes; source review plus measured outputs, not a causal component ablation.

rows.rationale:
Deep ensemble of ResNet-9 CNNs for the 12k-row Fashion-MNIST subset:
longer per-member cosine schedules, diversified per-sample augmentation,
optional mixup, and multi-view (shift + flip) test-time augmentation.

Rationale (exploratory; the common reference is a single ResNet-9 trained
~100 epochs with batch-level crop/flip, dev error 0.068; a first ensemble
attempt with 8 members x 72 epochs and heavy affine+cutout augmentation
scored 0.0685, i.e. no gain).  Two concrete hypotheses about that null
result drive this method:

 1. Under-training of members.  That run consumed only 173 s of its 640 s
    budget because the per-member epoch count was hard-capped at 72; with
    strong per-sample augmentation each member was very likely weaker than
    the 100-epoch reference, so the ensemble merely recovered the reference
    level.  Here the epoch count is derived from the *measured* step time so
    that the whole training budget is actually spent (typically ~200 epochs
    per member), and the cosine schedule always anneals to zero.

 2. Too little useful diversity / too aggressive a single augmentation
    policy.  Members now use different augmentation strengths and half of
    them additionally use mixup, which both regularises long schedules and
    decorrelates member errors; softmax averaging then converts the
    decorrelation into an accuracy gain.

Test-time augmentation is extended from {identity, hflip} to 5 translations
x {identity, hflip} (10 views), which is essentially free at prediction time
and matches the translation range used during training.

Limitations: no labelled internal validation is performed (all 12k rows feed
every member), so reported member accuracies are in-sample and optimistic;
the ensemble gain is assumed from the mechanism above, not measured against
labels here.  Development features are used only for an unlabeled
disagreement diagnostic - never for fitting or pseudo-labelling - so that the
development estimate stays comparable to confirmation/audit behaviour.

measured_findings.augmentation: per-sample affine (rot 6-12deg, scale +-6-10%, shift +-0.10-0.14), hflip, cutout 6-10px p=0.5; mixup alpha=0.2 on half the members
measured_findings.tta: 5 translations x {identity, hflip}, softmax averaged over members
measured_findings.limitations: no labelled internal validation; every member sees all training rows, so member accuracies are in-sample/optimistic; ensemble gain is a mechanism assumption, not a labelled measurement here. Development features used only for unlabeled disagreement statistics, never for fitting.

audit.uncertainty_note: Paired group bootstrap, descriptive rather than a finite-sample guarantee.

rows.rationale:
Ensemble refinement of the fashion reference. The rationale is exploratory and unverified.

Reference: one residual CNN, SGD with cosine schedule, crop and flip, dev error 0.068.
Target: error <= 0.0612.

Proposal:
1. Keep the parent (reference) network as one ensemble member. It is loaded from
   api.parent_dir/model.pkl, so it costs no training time.
2. Train up to 3 more networks of the same architecture with different seeds and
   stronger augmentation:
   - per-sample random translation (the reference used one crop offset per batch);
   - horizontal flip;
   - cutout.
   Each member gets a time-budgeted cosine schedule.
3. Predict by averaging softmax probabilities over members, each with flip TTA.

Hypothesis: ensembling decorrelated members plus better augmentation reduces
variance-dominated error in the 12k-sample regime.

Limitations:
- There is no labelled validation data in training.
- Findings report only timing, epochs, training fit, and agreement on dev features.

measured_findings.method: parent + new-member softmax ensemble with flip TTA
measured_findings.limitations: No labelled internal validation. Agreement is not accuracy. Members share the architecture and train split.

audit.uncertainty_note: Paired group bootstrap, descriptive rather than a finite-sample guarantee.

rows.rationale:
Fashion-MNIST: grow the b0-s0 ensemble. b0-s0 (3x ResNet9, translate+flip+
cutout, SGD cosine, EMA, flip-TTA) reached 6.15% dev error, missing the 6.12%
target by one image, while using only 275 of 690 training seconds (epoch cap
hit). Ensembling is the most reliable variance reducer here, so this step loads
the parent's three trained nets from api.parent_dir (falls back to training
from scratch if unavailable) and trains 4 further members with the same recipe
but a longer schedule (cap 220 epochs, time-bounded), then averages softmax of
all members with flip TTA. Unverified expectation: 7 members vs 3 shave a few
tenths of a percent. No dev labels used; no internal held-out estimate.

measured_findings.recipe: parent ResNet9 EMA nets + new members (translate pad3, flip, cutout12, SGD nesterov cosine, EMA 0.998, up to 220 epochs), softmax averaging with flip TTA
measured_findings.limitations: no held-out labels used; train accuracy is on fitted rows and optimistic; no group-respecting internal validation; gain over 3-member parent is unverified

audit.uncertainty_note: Paired group bootstrap, descriptive rather than a finite-sample guarantee.

rows.rationale:
Powerplant (CCPP) regression: push past the single-HGB reference (dev MSE 9.94) and the
tree+isotropic-kernel blend parent (dev MSE 9.42, only ~5% reduction).

Rationale (exploratory, validated only by grouped out-of-fold estimates):
  * The parent's kernel bases were isotropic in standardized 4-d space (OOF 14.9/16.6),
    which is a poor metric here: ambient temperature and exhaust vacuum carry almost all
    signal while pressure/humidity are weak and noisy. An ARD (per-feature lengthscale)
    kernel ridge, tuned by coordinate descent on grouped CV with exact GPU fp64 Cholesky
    solves, should be a far stronger *smooth* base and therefore a much better complement
    to axis-aligned tree ensembles.
  * Tree ensembles pay a piecewise-constant approximation penalty on this smooth response
    surface. A locally weighted linear regression (tricube-weighted k-NN ridge on the ARD
    metric) removes exactly that first-order bias and is cheap in closed form, so it is
    added as a second smooth, strongly decorrelated base.
  * All bases get grouped out-of-fold predictions (declared protocol) and are combined by
    non-negative least squares with intercept, with a guard that never accepts a blend
    worse than the best single OOF base.

Limitations: blend weights and all hyper-parameters are selected on grouped OOF
predictions of the same training split, so reported OOF MSEs are internal and mildly
optimistic; no development labels are used anywhere. Every optional component is time
guarded and wrapped, falling back to the tuned tree ensemble alone.

measured_findings.limitations: all hyper-parameters and blend weights selected on grouped OOF predictions of the same training split (internal, mildly optimistic); no development labels used; kernel search is a greedy coordinate descent under a time cap, not exhaustive.

audit.uncertainty_note: Paired group bootstrap, descriptive rather than a finite-sample guarantee.

rows.rationale:
Powerplant: stacked ensemble of heterogeneous regressors (unverified exploratory rationale).

The reference is HistGradientBoosting (dev MSE 9.94); the target is about 8.94.
The inputs are four smooth physical variables, and the response surface is smooth
and low-dimensional. Tree models approximate it piecewise. Smooth models should
capture it better:
  - an exact Gaussian process on the GPU, with an ARD RBF + Matern52 kernel and
    marginal-likelihood hyperparameters;
  - a batched MLP ensemble.
These are combined with HGB (the reference config), ExtraTrees and kNN.
Blend weights are nonnegative least squares on GroupKFold out-of-fold predictions,
using api.train_groups.

Findings report measured per-model OOF MSE and the blend weights.
Limitation: the blend OOF MSE is slightly optimistic because the weights were fit
on the same OOF predictions.

measured_findings.limitations: Single seed; blend weights fit on the same OOF predictions; dev/audit performance not measured here.

audit.uncertainty_note: Paired group bootstrap, descriptive rather than a finite-sample guarantee.

rows.rationale:
Powerplant regression, refinement of b1-s0 (dev MSE 9.655 vs reference 9.938).

Hypothesis: the b1-s0 stack gained ~3% mostly by mixing three near-identical HGB variants
(weights concentrated there; ET/RF/kNN/MLP were near-useless). Further variance reduction
needs bases that are strong AND decorrelated from deterministic HGB. This step adds
(a) physically motivated monotone HGB (PE decreases with AT, V, RH; increases with AP),
(b) stochastic subsampled sklearn GBR ensembles (squared and Huber loss, seed-averaged),
(c) an exact ARD Matern-3/2 Gaussian process fitted on GPU (float64) by marginal
likelihood - a smooth non-tree model class. Weights are NNLS on GroupKFold OOF
predictions; the stack is selected only if OOF MSE beats every base and the uniform mean.
Weak bases from b1-s0 (kNN, MLP, et_fe) are dropped. Unverified: transfer of OOF gain to
development/audit; the exact reference recipe stays as a base so findings report an
internal OOF relative reduction. All learned state is stored in the model dict.

measured_findings.limitations: Relative reduction is a train-only OOF estimate on the same split as the reference; no development labels used. Stack weights fitted on the OOF used for selection (mild optimism). Transfer to development/audit unverified; monotone constraints are a physical assumption that may be violated locally.

audit.uncertainty_note: Paired group bootstrap, descriptive rather than a finite-sample guarantee.

rows.rationale:
Newsgroups method: diverse linear-model ensemble over word + char TF-IDF, with an
optional transductive self-training refit performed at prediction time.

Rationale (parts are exploratory, validated only on an internal group-aware holdout):
- The two reference candidates (word 1-2gram LinearSVC = 0.2864 dev error, char
  3-5gram LinearSVC = 0.2940) are close in accuracy but use disjoint feature
  spaces, so their errors should be partly decorrelated.  A score-level ensemble
  of word-SVC, char-SVC, a union-feature SVC and ComplementNB is the cheapest way
  to exploit that diversity; weights are chosen on a GroupShuffleSplit holdout
  (grouping = api.train_groups, i.e. normalized subject threads) rather than by
  guesswork.
- TF-IDF vocabulary/IDF is fit on train+development *features only* (no labels),
  which is permitted and improves vocabulary coverage of the evaluation domain.
- Self-training: at predict time the whole evaluation split is available, so the
  ensemble scores are used to pseudo-label the most confident portion of it and a
  union-feature SVC is refit on labeled + down-weighted pseudo-labeled data.  This
  is enabled only if it reduced error on the internal holdout (treated as an
  unlabeled pool), otherwise it is disabled and the plain ensemble is returned.
Limitations: a single 20% group holdout (~2k docs) is a noisy selector for blend
weights and for the self-training decision; gains measured there may not fully
transfer.  No pretrained representations are used.

measured_findings.limitations: single 20% group holdout selects blend weights and the self-training switch; development/audit performance not measured here

audit.uncertainty_note: Paired group bootstrap, descriptive rather than a finite-sample guarantee.

rows.rationale:
Transductive word+char TF-IDF ensemble with group-validated self-training (newsgroups).

Rationale (exploratory, unverified until measured): the reference is a word (1,2)-gram
TF-IDF LinearSVC with 0.286 development error. With headers, quotes and footers
removed, many posts are short, so three changes are tried together:
  1. Character n-grams (char_wb 2-5) are added to the word n-grams. They are more
     robust to rare words, misspellings and morphology.
  2. The SVM margins are blended with ComplementNB scores, after standardizing each
     row of scores. The blend weight is chosen on a group holdout.
  3. Transductive learning. IDF and vocabulary are fitted on labeled plus unlabeled
     text (the stored development text plus the features being predicted). Then two
     rounds of confident pseudo-label self-training are run. No labels are used for
     the unlabeled rows.
Training runs a GroupShuffleSplit holdout using api.train_groups (20% of training
groups) to choose among these options. The chosen option is refit inside predict on
all training data, using the prediction features as unlabeled data. The training
text and labels are stored in the model for that refit.
Limitations: the holdout has about 2k documents (SE roughly 1%). The choice uses the
same train/dev split history as the reference.

measured_findings.limitations: Single group holdout (~20% train groups), SE about 1%; transductive refit happens in predict using features as unlabeled data.

audit.uncertainty_note: Paired group bootstrap, descriptive rather than a finite-sample guarantee.

rows.rationale:
Repair of b0-s0 (KeyError: 'nb' -- the ComplementNB member had no feature matrix mapped).
Newsgroups reference: word TF-IDF LinearSVC, ~28.6% dev error. Design unchanged: word (1,2)-gram
and char_wb (2,5)-gram TF-IDF vectorizers fit unsupervised on train + unlabeled development text;
LinearSVC members on word / char / concatenated features plus ComplementNB on word TF-IDF.
C values and blend weights of row-centred, std-normalised scores are chosen by GroupKFold
out-of-fold error on api.train_groups (subject groups). Changes vs parent: NB maps to the word
matrix, 3 folds instead of 4 and a reordered, time-capped member schedule (previous run spent
~430 s on 12 fits, the concatenated matrix being the slowest), so the run fits the 900 s limit.
Findings: OOF error per member and for the selected blend (development-label independent).

measured_findings.limitations: OOF errors use 3-fold GroupKFold on training groups only; blend weights were selected on the same OOF scores (mild optimism). Vectorizers saw unlabeled development text (IDF/vocabulary only). Members not finished within the time cap are absent from oof_error.

audit.uncertainty_note: Paired group bootstrap, descriptive rather than a finite-sample guarantee.
